The port refuses where Python answers: lines through the probe that pass within a few microns of a solid face's boundary keep an odd crossing count after the nudges, so the rays cannot place them, and the probe is not answered (before, those lines were read as air). Observed on mfcadpp/10255 #0 (lines along x within 5e-6 of the tangent of the recess's radius-1 wall, each crossing the solid five times) and nist_ctc_03 _recess_reduce #5 (lines 2.6e-6 above the z = 76.2 face the probe is inset from). A limitation of the ray caster's boundary handling, not of the probe.
